entries.title: Ed Sheeran admits 'mistakes' as he addresses Macklemore controversy

entries.snippet: Denmark and the US have reached an agreement after months of threats from Donald Trump to annex the territory.

entries.title: Our head teacher was an abuser. We joined forces to get justice - now we're married

entries.snippet: CNN, MS NOW and Politico reporters' White House press badges were confiscated, the outlets reported.

entries.title: Cultural treasures are being destroyed by war, and people want justice
entries.snippet: A cauldron of conflicts is bubbling across the world, with cultural monuments being destroyed. These people are fighting against it.

entries.title: Converse pulls 'deeply upsetting' advert after backlash
entries.snippet: Social media users say an image from the brand's Instagram account resembled a KKK hood and hanging.

entries.title: Trump says US will form 'AI Force' and appoint an artificial intelligence tsar
entries.snippet: The president said his administration "will not in any way hinder or stifle the growth" amid amid warnings about the emergent technology.

entries.title: Google's Gemini AI hacked three companies in security test
entries.snippet: The AI model accessed the internet and guessed credentials to three websites, a Google official told the BBC.

entries.title: Trump signs sweeping Russia sanctions bill
entries.snippet: The bill is named after the late Senator Lindsey Graham, a staunch advocate of aid for Ukraine.

entries.title: Grim discoveries of murdered women spark fear in South Africa
entries.snippet: Dineo Motapane is one of nine recent victims whose deaths have left a nation traumatised over the level of violence against women.

entries.title: Shark attack prompts rare kill order in Western Australia as victim named
entries.snippet: Greg O'Neill "loved the ocean", his family say, as police boats and helicopters patrol Perth's beaches in search of his body and the shark that attacked him.

entries.title: Millions without power as Cuba hit by latest major blackout
entries.snippet: Widespread power outages have become increasingly common due to fuel shortages made worse by a US blockade.

entries.title: At least 21 killed after vehicle loaded with explosives rams Pakistan mosque
entries.snippet: A four-year-old child is among those killed in the attack, during which gunmen also opened fire on a police facility.

entries.title: Mum's viral barefoot race sparks debate over India's education crisis
entries.snippet: Unprepared and in flip-flops, the 47-year-old widow ran 3km to try secure her daughter's future.

entries.title: Not all AI workers think the tech could kill everyone
entries.snippet: In text exchanges and conversations, multiple people who have worked for leading companies are sceptical of the warnings.

entries.snippet: The children of key politicians jailed 25 years ago without a trace in Eritrea want answers.

entries.title: A four-minute warning isn't enough: Russia's new relentless missile tactics exhaust Kyiv residents
entries.snippet: Increasingly frequent and ferocious attacks on the Ukrainian capital have left many on edge.

entries.title: I found love at an Irish matchmaking festival - and I want others to do the same
entries.snippet: Mary Timby flew to Ireland on a whim last year and met her boyfriend at a matchmaking festival.

entries.title: Tata Sons: India's corporate crown braces for upheaval amid boardroom revolt
entries.snippet: The Tata boardroom battle has intensified over a re-appointment of its chairman and a diktat to go public.

entries.title: The new lines of southern Lebanon
entries.snippet: The U.N. expanded the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon's mandate 20 years ago to include monitoring adherence to a ceasefire in fighting between Israel and Lebanon's Iran-backed Hezbollah — the militant group created in 1982 to counter a second Israeli invasion.

entries.title: CNN, MS NOW, Politico reporters denied access to White House following Trump ban
entries.snippet: Three reporters were blocked from the White House grounds Saturday morning, a day after President Trump said CNN, Politico, and MS NOW would be banned for reporting "FICTION and LIES."

entries.title: Opinion: Remembering Annie Dillard, nature writer
entries.snippet: With her 1974 book, "Pilgrim at Tinker Creek," Annie Dillard became the youngest woman to win the Pulitzer Prize. We take a moment to remember her and her work.

entries.title: Life in Kabul 5 years after the Taliban's return
entries.snippet: Five years after the return of Taliban rule, NPR visited Kabul to see how Afghans are dealing with their new government's strict social restrictions.

entries.title: Betel nuts are a top mind-affecting substance. Now there's evidence of ancient use
entries.snippet: New research on ancient human remains suggests the habitual usage of betel nuts, a plant seed with mind-affecting properties that is popular in parts of Asia despite the health risks it presents.

entries.title: Archaeologists are racing to save precious artifacts in Alaska after last year's storm
entries.snippet: Last year, remnants of a typhoon damaged homes, infrastructure and an archaeological dig site. Now, archaeologists are trying to get as many objects out as possible before the next storm.

entries.title: Ever wonder how the Fed's interest rate actually works? We've got answers
entries.snippet: The Federal Reserve just raised interest rates this week for the first time this year. So how does it actually work? And what does it mean for the economy — and the rest of us? Here are some answers.

entries.title: Russia holds parliamentary vote in areas it seized from Ukraine in the war
entries.snippet: Russia's parliamentary election for the first time is being held in Ukraine's regions that Moscow illegally annexed after the start of its full-scale invasion more than 4 1/2 years ago.

entries.title: As Europe warms, Italy sees West Nile virus spread
entries.snippet: Italian health authorities see evidence that rising temperatures and longer warm seasons are helping mosquitoes spread West Nile virus across a wider area, during more months of the year.

entries.title: U.S. and Denmark reach deal to build U.S. military presence in Greenland
entries.snippet: President Trump says he has a deal with Denmark to bolster the U.S. military presence in Greenland. The announcement comes after months of threatening to take the island by force from the NATO ally.

entries.title: For Palestinian aid groups, Macklemore's $1M pledge brings relief and attention to ongoing suffering
entries.snippet: Macklemore committed to donate his net earnings from Ed Sheeran's Loop Tour after he was dropped for making pro-Palestinian comments onstage at New Jersey's MetLife Stadium.

entries.title: Saudi Arabia confirms Yemen's Houthi rebels tried to attack its capital with a ballistic missile
entries.snippet: The growing conflict near another important global shipping corridor has brought new pressures for markets.

entries.title: Michigan city defends itself against accusations of favoring Muslim holidays over other faiths
entries.snippet: A statement from the Detroit suburb issued by a spokesperson came in response to a lawsuit on Thursday that accused the city and its mayor of spending thousands of dollars to celebrate Muslim holidays while ignoring Christian and Jewish holidays.

entries.title: Congo begins Ebola vaccinations for health workers in the epicenter of the outbreak
entries.snippet: Health workers and other front-line workers in the Ebola response are being prioritized to receive the Ervebo vaccine that was effective in past Ebola outbreaks caused by a different, more common type of virus.

entries.title: Russian election observer loses consciousness during arrest by police, opposition party says
entries.snippet: The three-day election, which began Friday and ends Sunday, features virtually no opposition and is all but certain to secure the Kremlin's political dominance.

entries.title: Denmark's leaders are cautiously optimistic about Trump's announcement of a Greenland deal
entries.snippet: U.S., Greenlandic and Danish officials had quietly negotiated for months behind the scenes, searching for solutions to address some of Trump's security concerns about the territory.

entries.title: Lawsuit says Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceXAI and Google made illegal agreement on AI slowdown
entries.snippet: The lawsuit argues that the leading AI companies violated antitrust laws when they agreed to coordinate slowdown efforts, and that doing so would reduce the value consumers get for paid AI subscriptions.

entries.title: Dodgers owner Mark Walter sued over alleged failure to disclose federal probe to policyholders
entries.snippet: Walter has been under investigation since last year by the U.S. Attorney's Office in Manhattan and the Securities and Exchange Commission following a whistleblower complaint regarding alleged misrepresented loans made between companies within his business portfolio.

entries.title: Trump announces all 50 states joining Medicaid drug pricing model
entries.snippet: The Trump administration claims that Medicaid will save billions on prescription drug costs as a result of the plan, dubbed the Medicaid "GENEROUS" model. Experts say the savings are unclear since the content of the deals isn't public.

entries.title: MS NOW, CNN and Politico say their journalists were denied access to White House after Trump ban
entries.snippet: The actions were a clear escalation of Trump's long-running efforts — in the courts and through administrative action — to restrict news coverage by journalists he finds objectionable.

entries.title: Thousands join protest outside Kennedy Center, expressing concern that Trump might tear it down
entries.snippet: Friday's event followed a tumultuous week in federal courts in Washington where filings and counter-filings flooded the courts as the administration continues pushing for the president's vanity projects.

entries.title: Trump administration begins building border wall in Big Bend region of Texas
entries.snippet: The start of construction marks an important milestone in the administration's $46 billion plan to line the border with walls, barriers, roads and technology as it seeks to make good on a key campaign promise by Trump to finish the wall.

entries.title: What's in the Greenland agreement between U.S. and Denmark
entries.snippet: On Friday, President Trump declared a deal has been struck with Denmark over its oversight of Greenland. Trump has long coveted the mineral-rich island, which Denmark has controlled since the 1700s. Nick Schifrin reports.

entries.title: Trump says he's banning 3 outlets from White House in his latest attack on press freedom
entries.snippet: President Donald Trump says he is banning three major news outlets, CNN, MS NOW and Politico, from the White House due to what he called "unfavorable coverage." Trump didn't provide details on how the ban would be implemented, but warned he might bar other media outlets as well.

entries.title: News Wrap: Newsom signs order for AI safety in California

entries.title: 'Shadow surge' pushes immigration arrests to highs as Trump administration shifts tactics

entries.title: Meet Earth's newest wild cat species, living in Bolivia and the first named in over a century
entries.snippet: A previously unknown cat species has been identified in plain sight: at a wildlife sanctuary in Bolivia, where the small, spotted feline had been living for years after being taken in by a local family.

entries.title: U.S.-Saudi nuclear power deal faces pushback over potential weapons risks

entries.title: What's making the Texas Senate race so competitive

entries.title: Capehart and Ponnuru on Trump's attacks on press freedom

entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Summer of 2026 broke records in Europe, and caused deaths
entries.snippet: The summer of 2026 was not only the hottest on record in Europe, it also saw a record number of people die. More than 16,000 are thought to have died because of the heat in Germany alone.

entries.title: Trump announces new 'AI force' amid mounting pressure
entries.snippet: Several voices, including from within the AI industry, have been calling for policing the fast-growing technology. Trump has once again called AI warnings "hoaxes" and vowed to "cherish, help" the industry.

entries.title: German-Russian relations at freezing point
entries.snippet: Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine destroyed the once-close relationship between Moscow and Berlin. Yet the far-right AfD is calling for a normalization of relations.

entries.title: Ukraine steps up measures to protect railways
entries.snippet: As Russia increases its attacks on Ukraine's rail infrastructure, the Ukrainian government has called for help to replace destroyed locomotives and is making plans to keep passengers safe.

entries.title: CNN, MS NOW and Politico denied access to White House
entries.snippet: Three US news outlets said their journalists were blocked from entering the White House grounds, hours after President Donald Trump announced bans on several media outlets.

entries.title: Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania: Will economy shape the vote?
entries.snippet: Voters in the eastern state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania head to the polls on Sunday, with the Social Democrats and far-right AfD neck and neck. Here's a look at key economic issues that could influence the election.

entries.title: Saudi Arabia: Houthis claim strikes on Riyadh, Yanbu port
entries.snippet: The Yemen-based Houthis said they targeted "sensitive sites" in Riyadh, hours after a blaze at a fuel depot near the Saudi capital's main airport. The Saudi-led coalition said Saudi defense downed a ballistic missile.

entries.title: Drone sightings briefly shut Luxembourg airport
entries.snippet: Flights were diverted and hundreds of passengers affected after unauthorized drones appeared near Luxembourg's only international airport.

entries.title: Thousands protest Kennedy Center demolition fears
entries.snippet: Protesters took part in a "Hands Around the Kennedy Center" human chain. The demonstration comes amid fears the Trump administration could tear the arts hub down.

entries.title: Oktoberfest 2026: Everything you need to know
entries.snippet: This year, AI will be used to manage overcrowded situations. Find all the numbers surrounding the fest — including the price of water!

entries.title: Rebels, workers, radicals: The making of 'Red Berlin'
entries.snippet: Bloody May, student sit-ins and the squatter movement: Berlin has long been a hotbed for working-class organizing and radical left-wing politics.

entries.title: Ed Sheeran continues US tour amid Palestinian controversy
entries.snippet: Pro-Palestinian protests are expected at Ed Sheeran's first gig since Macklemore was dropped from the tour. The US rapper shouted "Free Palestine" at a concert in New Jersey.

entries.title: Oktoberfest opens as Munich mayor taps first beer keg
entries.snippet: Thousands of visitors streamed onto Munich's Oktoberfest grounds as the world-famous beer festival got underway. Some spent the night outside the gates to secure coveted places in the festival tents.

entries.title: US court rejects Trump policy on third-country deportations
entries.snippet: The Trump administration has deported more than 25,000 people to countries other than their own. Now a federal appeals court has put the brakes on the policy.

entries.title: India news: British Sikh activist Jagtar Singh Johal granted bail after 9 years in detention
entries.snippet: Sikh activist Jagtar Singh Johal has been granted bail after more than eight years without conviction. Meanwhile, India swapped its male flagbearer for the Asian Games opening ceremony over a missing kit. DW has more.

entries.title: Russia votes for new parliament in controlled elections
entries.snippet: Russia is holding its first State Duma election since invading Ukraine, with voting also imposed in occupied Ukrainian regions. President Vladimir Putin's party is expected to dominate the tightly controlled contest.

entries.title: Germany news: Campaigns wrap up in two state elections
entries.snippet: Parties are campaigning for a last day ahead of polls in Mecklenburg-Vorpomerania and Berlin. And an association responsible for German sea ports says they are at high risk from cyberattacks and sabotage. DW has more.

entries.title: Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania: SPD seeks to fend off AfD
entries.snippet: For nearly three decades, the Social Democrats have governed Germany's northeastern state. If they can fend off the AfD, the result may boost the fortunes of the German government's junior coalition partner.

entries.title: Pakistan: Suicide bombing death toll rises to at least 31
entries.snippet: More than 100 others have been injured in the militant attack on a police headquarters near the border with Afghanistan. Several militants were still clashing with Pakistan's security forces on Saturday.
